name: SISO Compute Pool · Free Qwen Worker Tier
summary: A controller that serves Qwen3.8-27B on free Kaggle TPU sessions behind a private Bifrost gateway, so agents gain a zero-cost worker tier. Transport is a Cloudflare Worker relay the notebook dials out to, because the account holds no zone. The delivery path is verified end-to-end against a mock origin; no TPU allocation, model throughput or output quality has been measured, and continuous service is not established.

evidence.summary: Private owning repository and pushed documentation commit verified on branch codex/vps-single-pilot-handoff. Reviewed the controller, readiness gates, relay worker and client, and the dated progress record. No private source payload, credential or account identity is distributed by this Work.

license.reason: Public metadata only. The private source, credentials and account identities receive no redistribution grant from this registration.

relationships.context: Shares the agent-effectiveness programme's evidence discipline; this project supplies a candidate zero-cost worker tier to it.

evidence.summary: The progress record states the intended consumer of the worker tier and the limits that bound it.

From the OVH VPS against a mock origin: probe returned ready true, register returned registered true with gateway_verified true, and one chat completion traversed Bifrost and the Cloudflare relay in 373 ms with a Cf-Ray header. Relay auth rejects an absent key with 401 and an absent worker with 503; streaming relays frame by frame and reconnects after client loss. This is transport evidence only.

Kaggle permits one concurrent TPU session per account, refused at push time rather than queued, with a roughly nine hour session cap and a twenty hour weekly quota. Observed cold start is 25 to 50 minutes and one probe queued 44 minutes. Queued kernels consume no quota, so a successor can be pre-queued, but overlap requires a second account. Unattended use is therefore a bounded batch, not continuous service.

Qwen has never served a token under this controller. TPU allocation, model startup, sustained throughput and output quality remain unmeasured. Readiness gate one exists because Kaggle has previously returned CPU silently in place of a requested accelerator.
